reference: Canonical M. tuberculosis resistance pharmacology, checked against the WHO catalogue of mutations v2
note: Locus tags in H37Rv nomenclature. A failure here is not always a bug: the WHO catalogue is versioned, and a locus regraded upstream will change what the classifier can say. Read a failure as 'the sources no longer support this expectation' and check which changed.

rules.why: rpoC is the canonical rifampicin compensatory locus: rpoB resistance mutations impair RNA polymerase and rpoC changes restore fitness. Both are RNA polymerase subunits, so the functional link should carry evidence beyond literature co-mention.
katG's day job is oxidative defence, so losing it weakens peroxide detoxification; ahpC promoter upregulation compensates. ahpC is catalogued under isoniazid with no graded-associated variant.

rpoA is a rifampicin compensatory locus and was never assessed against isoniazid, so it cannot be compensating for katG. The catalogue-shape test alone would call this compensation, and STRING will supply a weak co-mention edge to support it.
MDR-TB is defined as resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin. These co-occur because the isolate received both drugs, not because the loci are related.
Two loci conferring resistance to the same drug. Isoniazid selects either, so they co-occur under one drug's pressure rather than through a relationship.

Resistance while katG matches the reference: the fabG1-inhA promoter route taken instead. The interval carries the catalogue's inhA c.-770/-777/-778/-779 variants, which sit physically between Rv1482c and fabG1 despite being named for inhA.
The dominant isoniazid mechanism on its own. Recovers known pharmacology and should not be flagged as anything more.
inhA is graded for isoniazid and ethionamide: one mechanism covering two drugs, because ethionamide is also a prodrug hitting InhA.
A known rifampicin locus varying in susceptible isolates. Either the variant is not one of the graded ones, is suppressed, or is a calling artefact -- all worth surfacing.
fabG1 is absent from the WHO catalogue, so it was never assessed. Must read as unknown rather than as a negative.
A known mechanism with something unexplained beside it. Both facts must survive, and the unexplained one must lead so the rule lands in a bucket a reviewer opens.
Fluoroquinolone and pyrazinamide resistance loci. Different drugs, so treatment history rather than any relationship between the loci.
